title: Approach Not the Altar with Gloom in Thy Soul
description: Approach Not the Altar with Gloom in Thy Soul in Tonic Solfa to ST DENIO, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Frances Sargent Osgood wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 464, “Glad Worship”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Elevens (11.11.11.11), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST DENIO; any other Elevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ap-proach not the al-tar with gloom in thy soul, Nor let thy feet fal-ter from ter-ror's con-trol; God loves not the sad-ness of fear and mis-trust; O, serve Him with glad-ness, the Lov-ing and Just!

lines: Approach not the altar with gloom in thy soul,
Nor let thy feet falter from terror's control;
God loves not the sadness of fear and mistrust;
O, serve Him with gladness, — the Loving and Just!
His bounty is tender, His being is love;
His smile fills with splendor the blue arch above;
His courts with thanksgiving, His portals with praise!
Come not to His temple with pride in thy mien
But lowly and simple, in courage serene;
Bring meekly before Him the faith of a child,
Bow down and adore Him with heart undefiled!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Frances Sargent Osgood died in 1850.
credits: Words by Frances Sargent Osgood (1811–1850), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST DENIO by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
